 JUDGMENT

In this appeal, the petitioner has challenged the judgment and award dated 31.12.2015 in M.V.C.No.4205/2014 passed by the III Addl. Senior Civil Judge and M.A.C.T., Bengaluru (SCCH-18)
('the Tribunal' for short).

entities.text: III Addl. Senior Civil Judge and M.A.C.T., Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are, on 03.09.2014 at about 01:00 pm, the petitioner was hit by a motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-07/M-3431 while he was crossing the road near R.T.O. office on Old Madras Road, near S.J.E.S. College, Bengaluru, injuring him.

After taking treatment at Government Hospital, K.R. Puram and Bowring Hospital, Bengaluru under hospitalization, he approached the Tribunal for grant NC: 2023:KHC:41058 of compensation of Rs.8,00,000/-.
Claim was opposed by the Insurance Company.

The Tribunal after taking the evidence, attributed 20% contributory negligence against him and assessed a sum of Rs.2,95,500/- and awarded 80% of it i.e.,
Rs.2,34,000/- with 9% interest p.a.
Pleading inadequacy, seeking enhancement and questioning the attribution of 20% contributory negligence, he has filed this appeal on various grounds.
4. Heard the arguments of Sri. Suresh. M. Latur, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri. Krishna Kishore, learned counsel for the Insurance Company.

5. It is the contention of learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner has suffered multiple fractures of right leg, left ribs and pubic bone; he was under hospitalization for 23 days, laid-up for minimum of 6 months, spent huge money towards treatment, suffered disability of 36.5%;
the Tribunal NC: 2023:KHC:41058 did not consider these aspects and awarded the lesser compensation.

It is further contended that only for the reason of the petitioner was crossing the road, 20% contributory negligence is attributed erroneously, there is 100% negligence on part of the driver of the car, full compensation has to be awarded and he sought for enhancement.

6. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that after the treatment,
the petitioner became normal, there is no physical disablement; if the petitioner has crossed the road cautiously, there would not have been any accident; but for his negligence without observing the incoming traffic entering into the traffic, tailored the accident and he has to be attributed 50% of contributory negligence, however the Tribunal has taken a lighter view that the petitioner is a pedestrian; the compensation assessed by the Tribunal is proper, no banks will offer interest at 9%,

7. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on both sides and also perused the materials on record.
8.

sentences.text: There is no dispute as to the accident, cause of the accident, injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident.
Ex.P4/wound certificate and Ex.P8/discharge summary did point out that the petitioner has suffered  rd fracture of right tibia, fracture of 3rd and 4th left ribs and fracture of pubic rami.
Exs.P9 and P12/out-patient cards and Ex.P13/case sheet point out that the petitioner was under hospitalization for a period of 23 days.
Ex. P10
/ medical bills amounts to Rs.12,310/-.
The petitioner is aged 50 years, he is a Coolie (Mason) and he is said to have earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
The accident is of the year 2014.
The petitioner has not produced any material to explain NC: 2023:KHC:41058 that he was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
A person with no proof of income in the year 2014 will earn not less than Rs.8,500/- and accordingly, his income has to be assessed.
9. PW-2 Dr. S. Ramachandra is the treated Doctor, whose testimony points out that the petitioner has suffered whole body disability of 18% on account of the injuries.
Though the Tribunal has taken 13%, having regard to the fractures of right leg, left ribs and pelvis, it is proper to assess the disability at 15% instead of 13%.

The petitioner is claiming total compensation of Rs.5,66,000/-
under different heads.

Having regard to the gravity of the injury, it is proper to assess a sum of Rs.80,000/- towards pain and sufferings, Rs.12,500/- towards medical expenses, Rs.50,000/-
towards loss of amenities and discomfort, loss of income during laid- up for 6 months at Rs.8,500/-
comes to Rs.51,000/-, the medical evidence speaks of future medical NC: 2023:KHC:41058 requirement for which Rs.10,000/- is assessed, towards incidental expenses, Rs.20,000/- awarded by the Tribunal including attendant charges, travelling expenses, food and nourishment is kept intact.
As regarding loss of future earnings, the Tribunal assessed Rs.1,22,000/-.
As discussed above, the petitioner has suffered 15% disability, earning Rs.8,500/- per month, 10% has to be added towards future prospects, then the income comes to Rs.9,350/-.
As we are assessing future loss of income, it comes to Rs.9,350/- x 12 x '13' multiplier x 15% = Rs.2,18,790/-.

Thus in all, the petitioner is entitled to:

Total compensation comes to Rs.4,42,290/- as against Rs.2,92,500/-, thereby enhancement of Rs.1,49,790/-.
10. Now, the point is whether the petitioner is entitled to full compensation or attribution of contributory negligence at 20% is proper?
Ex. P3
/ spot sketch points out that the place of accident is a national highway which is called as 'Old Madras Road'.

The motor cycle was coming from K.R.
Puram towards Hoskote, it was 10 ft. inside the road from its left side, the petitioner has attempted to cross the road from northern to southern side and he did not observe the incoming traffic and all of a sudden entered the road.
This shows that the petitioner was not cautious and he was negligently crossed the road in spite of incoming traffic.

The rider of the motor cycle was pleaded guilty in NC:
2023:KHC:41058 C.C.No.3112/2014.
On this basis, complete negligence cannot be fastened against him.
The Court is required to consider all the aspects as to how the accident took place.
Hence, it is a fit case where contributory negligence has to be attributed against the petitioner.
The Tribunal has considered all the material on record while attributing contributory negligence, which does not call for interference.
Hence, out of enhanced compensation, the petitioner is entitled to 80% of it, which comes to Rs.1,19,832/-.
This is the just compensation that the petitioner is entitled to in the facts and circumstances of the case.

11. As regarding rate of interest is concerned, the Tribunal has exercised discretion in granting 9%
interest.
Since the Insurance Company has not filed any appeal, it is not proper to interfere with the discretion of the Tribunal.
Insofar as enhanced compensation is concerned, the petitioner is entitled - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:41058 to interest at 6% p.a.

Accordingly, the appeal merits consideration, in the result, the following:
ORDER i) Appeal is allowed-in-part.
ii) Impugned judgment and award is modified.
iii) Petitioner is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.1,19,832/- with interest of 6% p.a.

v) Amount in deposit, if any, shall be transmitted to the Tribunal along with records forthwith.
